h1: The 7 Best Monitor Arms of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: seven monitor arms from gas spring Ergotron models to budget clamp mounts, with weight limits, VESA support and screen sizes.
summary: The Ergotron LX is our best overall pick for its proven gas spring motion. The HUANUO TitanLift is the one for heavy ultrawides up to 49 inches. The HUANUO FlowLift is the value pick with a clamp and grommet base, and the ErGear is the cheapest way to try an arm.
intro: A monitor arm fails in a quiet way: it holds the screen fine on day one, then slowly droops because the weight range was wrong for your display. The listed capacity is not a ceiling you can push; it is a window, and both the low end and high end matter.

We reviewed eight arms and kept seven, setting one spring mount aside as too basic to rank. Scores reflect weight range, screen size, VESA support, mechanism, mounting options and price bucket, drawn from the spec sheets and owner feedback rather than bench work.

products.name: Ergotron LX Monitor Arm
products.verdict: The proven gas spring arm for standard and ultrawide screens.
products.description:
The Ergotron LX uses a gas spring for height and depth adjustment and supports flat, curved and ultrawide monitors up to 34 inches. It carries 7 to 25 pounds and fits VESA 75x75mm or 100x100mm in matte black.

It ranks first because its capacity range is wider than the budget FlowLift, and it sits in the $100-200 bucket for a recognised brand. The tradeoff against the TitanLift is size: it stops at 34 inches.

It suits most 21 to 34 inch setups. The caveat is the 7 pound minimum, so very light panels can bounce.
products.idealFor: Most desks with a 21 to 34 inch monitor.

products.name: HUANUO TitanLift Heavy Duty Monitor Arm
products.verdict: Holds up to 44 pounds and screens up to 49 inches.
products.description:
The TitanLift is an aluminum arm for screens up to 49 inches carrying up to 44 pounds, with a dual C-clamp base and a maximum VESA of 100x100mm.

It ranks second because it handles displays the Ergotron cannot, and it does so in the $50-100 bucket. It gives up the refined feel of the Ergotron brand.

The pick for large curved or gaming ultrawides. The caveat is that 100x100mm VESA may not match every 49 inch panel.
products.skipIf: You use a small, light monitor.

products.name: Ergotron LX Pro Premium Monitor Arm
products.verdict: A white finish and upgraded spring for long-term use.
products.description:
The LX Pro adds a premium upgraded gas spring and a white finish, supporting up to 34 inch monitors from 4 to 22 pounds on VESA 75x75mm or 100x100mm.

It ranks below the standard LX because its heavy end is lower at 22 pounds, though it handles lighter screens from 4 pounds. It stays in the $100-200 bucket.

Buy it for a white desk setup and lighter monitors. The caveat is the lower weight ceiling.
products.idealFor: Light monitors on a white desk.

products.name: HUANUO FlowLift Single Monitor Mount
products.verdict: Clamp and grommet bases in the box for a low price.
products.description:
The FlowLift fits 13 to 32 inch monitors weighing 4.4 to 19.8 pounds, with a clamp and grommet base both included. It offers tilt, swivel and rotation.

It ranks fourth because the capacity is lower than the Ergotron and the build is more modest. It sits in the $25-50 bucket, which is a big saving.

A sensible choice for a standard office monitor. The caveat is that ultrawides above 32 inches fall outside the range.

products.name: HUANUO FlowLift Pro Monitor Arm
products.verdict: A tool-free VESA mount for 20 to 27 inch screens.
products.description:
The FlowLift Pro offers a tool-free VESA mount, a C-clamp and grommet base, and a 19.8 pound limit for 13 to 32 inch screens. Tilt, swivel and rotation are included.

It ranks fifth because it matches the plain FlowLift on capacity, with the tool-free mount as its main addition. It stays in the $25-50 bucket.

It suits people who dislike fiddly installs. The caveat is that nothing in the listing improves on the weight limit.

products.name: WALI Single Monitor Mount
products.verdict: Holds 26.4 pounds, more than any other budget arm here.
products.description:
The WALI supports 13 to 34 inch screens, with a regular screen limit of 32 inches, and holds up to 26.4 pounds. It takes VESA 75 or 100mm and comes in black.

It ranks sixth because the listing is sparse on the clamp and mechanism, even though the capacity beats the FlowLift. It sits in the under $25 bucket.

Good for heavier mid-size monitors on a tight budget. The caveat is the thinner detail on build quality.
products.idealFor: Heavier monitors on a tight budget.

products.name: ErGear Single Monitor Arm
products.verdict: A tool-free arm with cable management at the lowest price.
products.description:
The ErGear fits 13 to 34 inch screens, holds 19.8 pounds and uses a tool-free VESA mount up to 100x100mm. Built-in cable management keeps wires tidy.

It ranks last because its capacity is lower than the WALI, though it matches the FlowLift models. It sits in the under $25 bucket.

A fair first arm. The caveat is the modest weight limit.

whatMatters.detail: Every arm has a minimum and maximum load. Too light a monitor makes the arm spring upward, while too heavy a monitor makes it sag. Find your screen's weight on its spec sheet and compare it with the arm's range.
VESA is the hole layout on the back of your display, usually 75x75mm or 100x100mm. If it does not match, the arm will not attach. Check your monitor's manual or the back panel.
Arms are rated by diagonal size. Ultrawides are wider and heavier than their number suggests. Check that your display falls inside the listed range.
Gas springs allow smooth motion with minimal force, while mechanical springs are simpler. This affects how easily you reposition the screen. Look for the mechanism name in the title or specs.
Clamps grip the desk edge, and grommet mounts pass through a hole. Thick or glass desks may not suit a clamp. Measure your desk thickness and check the arm's clamp range.

faq.q: How do I know if a monitor arm fits my monitor?
faq.a: Match the VESA pattern and the weight. Both must fall inside the arm's listed range.

faq.q: Can I mount a monitor without VESA holes?
faq.a: Not directly. Some monitors need an adapter bracket, so check your model first.

faq.q: Is a gas spring arm worth it?
faq.a: If you move the screen often, yes. For a fixed position, a basic arm is fine.

faq.q: Will a clamp damage my desk?
faq.a: It can mark soft surfaces. Use a pad if your desk is delicate.

faq.q: How do I fix a drooping arm?
faq.a: Adjust the tension screw, or check whether the monitor is too heavy for the arm.

faq.q: Can one arm hold two monitors?
faq.a: Only if it is designed for it. These are all single monitor arms.

finalTake: The Ergotron LX is the arm to buy for most desks, thanks to its smooth gas spring and wide screen support. If you own a very large ultrawide, the HUANUO TitanLift is the one that can carry it. On a tight budget the FlowLift gives the best mix of features.
